newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila communist hit squad vows to go nationwide.
newsitem.headline: Manila communist hit squad vows to go nationwide.

text.p: The Manila leftist death squad has decided to break away from the main communist group which is negotiating peace with the Philippine government and vowed to impose "revolutionary justice" nationwide, its leaders said on Sunday.

At a news conference held in its military camp in the central Negros Occidental province, Alex Boncayao Brigade (ABB) leader Sergio Romero said it had joined forces with the Revolutionary Proletarian Army, a group of former communist cadres in the central Philippines, to pursue their struggle towards a socialist state.
"As a revolutionary army, we place our forces at the disposal of the Filipino working class and revolutionary masses ... to advance the revolution," Romero said.

The ABB has shot dead several policemen and businessmen in broad daylight and at close range. Last June, it gunned down Rolando Abadilla, former head of the intelligence group formed by deposed president Ferdinand Marcos during the martial law.
Romero, vice commanding officer Lualhati Carapali and 50 of their armed men met local reporters weeks after the group's first congress near Bacolod city, 480 km (298 miles) south of Manila.
"We vow to punish abusive state agents and die-hard capitalists who've caused grave damage to the lives of the working masses," Romero said.
The group rejected the peace negotiations being pursued by the exiled communist leaders.
"Armed struggle remains a morally just and correct option of the masses of the people who aspire for social justice and a more humane society," Romero said.
At present, the leaders of the National Democratic Front are conducting peace talks with government representatives in the Dutch city of Utrecht.
The local insurgents have been operating since 1969.

The military says their strength has fallen to about 5,000 from a peak of more than 26,000 in the late 1980s because of the collapse of communism in Europe, battlefield losses and the surrender of many followers.
